content.text:
I submitted **index 18 (Cu 0.26 / Sb 0.74)** as the best composition. It had the highest efficiency (EQE) of the three I measured: **0.0132%**. The library has 29 compositions and all 3 EQE measurements are used, so the true best could be one I didn't test, most likely near index 18.

| Index | Cu / Sb | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 7 | 0.60 / 0.40 | −0.0002 (no photoactivity) |
| 16 | 0.31 / 0.69 | 0.0037 |
| 18 | 0.26 / 0.74 | **0.0132** |

- **Measurement choices:** I started with index 16 because it sits near CuSb2O6, the known copper–antimony oxide phase in this range. I tested index 7 to check the Cu-rich side, which turned out inactive.
- **What the X-ray scans show:** indices 13 and 16 are mostly CuSb2O6. By index 20 the film is mostly Sb oxide with a little CuSb2O6.
- **Why index 18:** the model's suggestion was index 20, but I skipped it because that film is mostly Sb oxide. I chose index 18 because it lies between the CuSb2O6 films and the Sb-oxide-rich one, where the two phases probably start to mix. I didn't scan index 18 itself, so that mixing is a guess. It gave about 3.6 times the EQE of index 16.

I used 3 of the 5 X-ray scans; 2 were left over.
